system_description.narrative_title: Global bond rout and rising yields reshaping markets
system_description.narrative_summary: A synchronized sell-off in global government bonds has pushed long-term yields to multi-year highs, driven by rising inflation, hawkish central-bank guidance and elevated oil prices. The repricing of 'risk-free' rates is transmitting across asset classes—lifting mortgage and borrowing costs, denting equities (especially interest-rate sensitive sectors), strengthening the dollar, and increasing stress on credit markets and fiscal financing. Market participants and policymakers are reacting in real time (auctions, Treasury moves, central-bank remarks), making the system highly dynamic and sensitive to data and geopolitical catalysts. The shock is creating knock-on effects for households, corporate funding, and political landscapes ahead of elections.
system_description.scope: Global sovereign bond markets and long-term yields; central-bank policy expectations; inflation and commodity (oil) drivers; investor positioning and liquidity; transmission to mortgage rates, corporate credit, equities, FX and safe-haven assets (gold).
system_description.super_system: Global macro-financial system and real economy (economic growth, inflation dynamics, fiscal policy and geopolitics).
adjacent_subsystems: Housing market and consumer credit (mortgages, affordability)
Banking sector, liquidity and derivatives markets
Energy/commodity markets (especially oil) and inflation pass-through

variables.name: Long-term nominal yields
variables.description: The prevailing market interest rate on long-dated sovereign bonds measured in nominal terms.

variables.name: Short-term policy rate expectations
variables.description: The market-implied expected path for short-term policy interest rates over the near to medium term.

variables.name: Inflation rate (headline)
variables.description: The observed rate of change in the general price level over a recent period.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The aggregate expected future rate of inflation over the medium-term as reflected in surveys and market prices.

variables.name: Real long-term yields
variables.description: Long-term interest rates adjusted for expected inflation, representing the real return on long-dated debt.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: The additional yield investors require to hold longer-maturity bonds versus rolling short maturities, independent of expected short rates.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price of crude oil reflecting energy cost pressures and commodity-driven inflation inputs.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: The ease, immediacy and cost of executing transactions in sovereign bond markets without large price impact.

variables.name: Investor risk aversion
variables.description: The aggregate preference of investors to avoid risk, influencing demand for safe versus risky assets.

variables.name: Credit spreads
variables.description: The yield premium demanded for non-sovereign credit over sovereign benchmarks, reflecting perceived credit and liquidity risk.

variables.name: Mortgage borrowing rates
variables.description: The average interest rate charged on long-term residential mortgage loans affecting household borrowing costs.

variables.name: Dominant currency strength
variables.description: The value of the major global funding currency in foreign-exchange markets relative to a broad basket of currencies.

variables.name: Equity valuation levels
variables.description: Aggregate market valuation metrics for equities (e.g., price-to-earnings ratios) indicating price relative to fundamentals.

variables.name: Corporate funding costs
variables.description: The effective interest rates and yield levels at which non-financial corporates can issue debt or obtain borrowing.

variables.name: Fiscal financing pressure
variables.description: The market-implied stress and cost of sovereign fiscal financing, including yield sensitivity to fiscal deficits and debt issuance needs.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: The level of price variability across financial markets measured by realized or implied volatility metrics.

catalysts.title: Possible Fed rate hike in October
catalysts.description: Markets and Fed officials signal a likely additional Fed policy move this year; a rate increase in October would directly shift rate expectations and yields.
catalysts.rationale: “Market sees next Fed hike in October”, “Fed's Williams says it is reasonable to see another US rate hike this year.”

catalysts.title: Upcoming US jobs and inflation releases
catalysts.description: Near-term employment and CPI/PCE data will test the Fed path and are likely to move short-rate expectations, yields and market volatility.
catalysts.rationale: “Wall St Week Ahead Jobs report, inflation data to test US rate path”, “Market sees next Fed hike in October.”

catalysts.title: Ongoing Treasury auction and supply pressure
catalysts.description: Strong supply and weak demand at recent auctions suggest continued issuance could keep upward pressure on yields and term premium.
catalysts.rationale: “Investors Demand Highest Yield at Two-Year U.S. Treasury Auction Since 2024”, “Why investors aren’t buying yet another attempt by the Treasury to calm the rattled bond market.”

catalysts.title: Volatile oil prices / energy shock risk
catalysts.description: Oil's recent moves (above $100 then retreating) create uncertainty for inflation and central‑bank policy; price direction will influence yields.
catalysts.rationale: “Global bond sell-off spreads as oil holds above $100”, “Global bond sell-off eases as oil prices retreat”, “Rate rise ‘increasingly likely’ if energy price shock persists.”

catalysts.title: Sustained mortgage rates above 7%
catalysts.description: Mortgage rates have breached 7%; persistence or further increases will feed through to housing affordability, credit and funding costs.
catalysts.rationale: “Mortgage Rates Just Hit 7%. Here’s How the Housing Market Is About to Change.”, “Bond rout pushes US mortgage rates past 7%.”

catalysts.title: Trump–Xi summit (geo‑political meeting)
catalysts.description: High‑profile summit between US and China leaders could change risk sentiment and safe‑haven flows, influencing bond yields and volatility.
catalysts.rationale: “Trump-Xi summit ahead; bond market selloff in focus - what’s moving markets”, “Trump Can Pressure the Fed - He Can’t Control Bond Yields.”
